name: Meal Planner
description: The family's meals for the week, day by day, with the groceries for them ordered on the family's grocery app, the everyday items and the family's recipe book; not for school runs, chores or appointments.

for: The family's meals for the week: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, day by day, each with its dishes
Groceries for the week's meals, ordered on the family's grocery app when they are needed
Everyday items (milk, curd, bread) ordered again and again on their own
The family's saved recipes, with their videos, planned into the week
notFor: School runs, chores or appointments (use checklist or tracker)
Keeping count of what is in the kitchen
A restaurant's menu or a business kitchen

settings.label: When something isn't on your main app

routines.name: Weekly meal plan
routines.description: Once a week, asks the agent to plan next week's meals and send the family the plan. On an install carried over from the old Meal Planner it first asks for the family's profile to be structured.

intents.name: sync-cart
intents.description: The family changed or opened their cart in Meal Planner: make the app's own cart match it.
intents.instructions: The payload has order_id, app and lines [{ item, product_id, name_on_app, qty }]. With that app's connector, make its cart hold exactly these lines (qty 0: take it off); touch only lines Meal Planner put there, and list any other line already in the cart as outside_lines. Read the cart back and call sync_cart { order_id, lines, total, delivery_gap, outside_lines }. Send no message.

operations.name: guide
operations.description: The full guide for working with this app: read it before the first conversation, a weekly plan, a check-in or an order. {}

operations.name: set_person
operations.description: Add or change one person who eats at home, found by name. { name, relationship?, group?: child | adult | elder, portions?, diet?, allergies?, dislikes?, targets?, note?, remove?: true }. group is needed for a new person. Keep portions, diet and the rest in the family's own words. Only the fields you send change; null clears one; remove: true takes the person out of the family.

operations.name: set_house_rules
operations.description: The house's food rules. { rules?: [{ kind: veg | egg | fasting | no_onion_garlic | other, days: ["Tue", "Thu"], note? }], notes?, structured?: true }. Send at least one of the three. The rules you send replace the ones there. The grocery app is not set here: use set_shopping_apps. A rule needs its days: weekdays, or the family's own word for a day ("Ekadashi"). Send structured: true once a profile carried over from the old app is fully in people, rules, the cook and slots, and at least one person is saved: it clears that text.

operations.name: set_cook
operations.description: The cook: who, which days, when they arrive, what they make well. { name, days: ["Mon", ...], arrival: "HH:MM", makes_well?, note? }. name, days and arrival are needed every time.

operations.name: set_slots
operations.description: Meals beyond Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, and the meals the family orders in every week. { extra_slots?: [{ name, days?: ["Mon", ...], for?: [names] }], order_in?: [{ day: "Sun", slot: "Dinner", note? }] }. Send at least one of the two; each list you send replaces the one there. An order_in slot is Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or an extra slot's name.

operations.name: set_cooking_days
operations.description: The days the family cooks at home. { days: ["mon", "tue", ...] }. At least one weekday; any capitals. A plan has meals on these days only; Mon to Sat until set. Answers { house }.

operations.name: set_shopping_apps
operations.description: The family's shopping apps. { main: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket | amazon, fallback: the app to try when something is not on the main one, or null, connected: [every app the family has signed in to] }. Apps by id or name ("Blinkit"). main and fallback are connected too, so need not be repeated; fallback must differ from main. Answers { main, fallback, connected, order_without_asking, house }.

operations.name: plan_week
operations.description: Plan a week of meals. { week_start: the week's Monday as YYYY-MM-DD, mode: draft | final, keep_rest?: true, meals?: [{ date, slot, ordered_in?: true, note?, dishes?: [{ name, for?: [names], portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }] }] }] }. Without meals it answers with the context to plan from (people, house, everyday items, last week's dishes, the recipe book), or, when mode is final and the week is a draft, makes that draft final. With meals they become the whole week's plan, in place of what was there; with keep_rest: true only the meals at the dates and slots you send are replaced and the rest of the week stays. A call carries 16 KB at most, so send a week one day a call: the first day with mode draft, each other day the same with keep_rest: true, then mode final without meals. A dish is for everyone unless you name who it is for; amount is a number above 0 with its measure in unit, for this family; an ordered-in meal has no dishes. Answers { week } or { context }.

operations.name: set_meal
operations.description: Change one meal, found by date and slot (or meal_id) and made when it is not there. { date, slot, or meal_id; ordered_in?, note?, dishes?: [as in plan_week] }. Only what you send changes; dishes you send replace the meal's dishes. ordered_in: true takes its dishes away; sending dishes with it is refused, and a meal that is ordered in takes dishes only with ordered_in: false. A meal keeps its date and slot. Answers { meal }.

operations.name: set_dish
operations.description: Add, change or remove one dish. { dish_id, or meal_id, or date and slot; name?, for?: [names], portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], position?, remove?: true }. Without dish_id, name is needed: in that meal a dish of the same name is the one changed; otherwise it is added at the end (and the meal made when it is not there). By dish_id a name you send renames it. Only what you send changes; ingredients you send replace the dish's; position 0 is first; for: null means everyone. Answers { dish, meal }; remove: true answers { meal }.

operations.name: set_regular
operations.description: Add or change one everyday item: what the house buys again and again whatever is cooked (milk, curd, bread, eggs). { item, amount, unit, every: day | week | weekdays, times_per_week?, weekdays?: ["Mon", ...], for_whom?, active?, paused_until?: YYYY-MM-DD, remove?: true }. amount (a number above 0), unit and every are needed for a new item. amount is what is needed each time: 1 l every day; 1 pack with every: week and times_per_week: 2; 6 pc with every: weekdays and weekdays: ["Mon"]. times_per_week is a whole number from 1 to 7 (1 when left out); weekdays is needed, with at least one day, when every is weekdays. Found by item and for_whom; only the fields you send change. paused_until leaves it out of the orders up to and including that date (a holiday); active: false stops it until you send active: true; remove: true deletes it. Set one only after the family confirmed it.

operations.name: import_order_history
operations.description: Give the app the family's past orders on one shopping app, one app a call. { app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket | amazon (by id or name), orders: [{ date: YYYY-MM-DD, order_ref?: the app's order id, items: [{ item, group?: daily | few_days | monthly, product?, product_id?, pack?: "5 kg", pack_amount?, pack_unit?, count?, price?, image? }] }] }. item is the family's word for it (atta), product the name on the app; count is how many packs (1 when left out). Send the most recent orders first, at most about 8 orders and 80 items a call, one app a call (a call carries 16 KB at most), and only the last 3 months: older orders are skipped. Each item becomes a purchase; the same order sent again is recorded once, so a call may overlap the last. An item with its product_id is remembered as that app's product. Answers { recorded, duplicates, skipped_old, needs_group: [items to give a group with set_item], suggestions: [everyday items to ask the family about, then set_regular], probably_out: [{ item, days_ago }] }.

operations.name: record_bought_outside
operations.description: The family bought an item outside the apps ("got atta from the kirana"). { item, date?: YYYY-MM-DD, today when left out }. It counts as a purchase of the usual amount and restarts the item's estimate. Answers { event_id } or { duplicate: true }, and { item }.

operations.name: set_item
operations.description: Change one item the family buys, made when it is not there. { item, group?: daily | few_days | monthly, follows_plan?: true when the week's meals use it up (paneer, rajma), dont_ask?: true to never ask about it, snooze_days?: days not to ask about it (null clears), unit?: g | kg | ml | l | pc }. Only what you send changes. Answers { item }.

operations.name: set_subscription
operations.description: An item delivered outside the apps (Country Delight, a milkman). { item, source: who delivers it, active: true | false }. active: true keeps it out of every cart and every question about running low, and takes it off the carts not yet ordered; active: false makes it an item like any other again. Answers { item }.

operations.name: answer_running_low
operations.description: The family's answers to "still in stock?". { answers: [{ item, answer: low | in_stock, days?: how many more days it will last }] }. low: it goes on the cart (answers { to_cart }). in_stock with days ("fine for a week": 7) is not asked again until then; in_stock without days ("still have it") waits a few days. Answers { to_cart: [items to add to the cart], items }.

operations.name: get_cart
operations.description: The carts: one open cart per shopping app, and any being ordered. { app?: one app by id or name }. Answers { carts: [{ order_id, app, app_name, status: open | ordering, lines: [{ id, item, qty, product_id, name_on_app, pack, price, source, for_note }], total, delivery_gap, sync_state, synced_at, outside_lines, building_at_order }] }. A line at qty 0 is shown, not ordered.

operations.name: set_cart_line
operations.description: Put an item on the cart, change its qty or take it off. { item, qty: packs, a whole number (0 takes it off), app?: the app (else the one the family buys it on, else the main app), source?: added (default) | low | everyday | meal, for_note?, product_id?, name_on_app?, pack?, price?, image? }. It goes on that app's open cart; while a cart is being ordered, a new item goes to a new open cart, and you may change or take off a line of the cart being ordered ("remove the ghee"). An item delivered outside the apps is refused (code SUBSCRIPTION). Copy the change to the app's own cart yourself in the same turn, then sync_cart. Answers { line, cart }.

operations.name: order_cart
operations.description: The family said yes to ordering one app's cart. { app }. The cart is being ordered from now on, and anything added later goes to a new cart. Send its message word for word, check out on the app, then record_order. Asked again while that order is being placed, it answers the same order. Answers { order_id, app, lines, message }; an empty cart is refused (409).

operations.name: sync_cart
operations.description: What the app's own cart holds after you copied a cart to it, or read it back. { order_id, lines: [{ product_id, qty, price?, in_stock?: false when the app does not have it today }], total?: the app's cart total, delivery_gap?: rupees short of free delivery, outside_lines?: [{ name, qty? }] (lines in the app's cart Meal Planner did not put there) }. Answers { cart }.

operations.name: record_order
operations.description: What happened to an order being placed. { order_id, placed?: true, paid?: true | false, app_order_ref?: the app's order id, total? }. placed: its lines become purchases and the items' estimates restart. paid: false (not paid): the purchases stop counting and the lines go back on the open cart; paid: true later brings both back. Send app_order_ref whenever you have it, also later. Answers { order }, and taken_off: [{ order_id, items }] when a late payment took returned items off a cart being ordered: take them off that checkout on the app too.

operations.name: cancel_order
operations.description: Stop an order. { order_id }. One being ordered goes back to the open cart (nothing was placed); a placed one counts as not paid, its lines back on the cart. Answers { order }.

operations.name: remember_product
operations.description: Remember the product an item is bought as on a grocery app, so the next order reuses it without searching. { item, app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket, product_id, name_on_app, pack?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }. item is the family's word for it, exactly as on the order line or the everyday item (milk), never the product's name on the app; pack_amount and pack_unit are the pack's size as a number and its measure (500, ml), which the app counts packs with (a plain pack text like "500 ml" is read too). One product per item and app: sending it again takes the place of the one remembered. Answers { product }.

operations.name: save_recipe
operations.description: Save a recipe, or change one. { recipe_id?, name?, links?: [the reel, short or page], notes?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], tags?: ["breakfast", "tiffin"], for?: [names], thumbnail? }. Without recipe_id, a recipe that already holds one of the links is the one changed (new links are added to it), so a link shared twice is saved once; otherwise a new recipe is made, and it needs a name: with none the answer is code NEEDS_NAME, so ask the family what to call it and save again. By recipe_id only what you send changes, and links you send replace its links. Answers { recipe }; put its id on a dish with set_dish recipe_id.

agentInterface.instructions: Meal Planner owns this family's profile, meals, everyday items, shopping and recipes. Read the app before you answer and change it only through its operations, then tell the family what the app now says. Call guide before a first conversation, a weekly plan, a check-in or an order. Save the family's own words; never fill anything from guesses. A shared reel plus "save this" is a save_recipe call.
